derivations.claim: Finite strings have a countable enumeration, so CH permits a kappa-list of all closed nowhere dense sets.
inputs: closed sets are recovered from their disjoint cylinders

derivations.claim: Strictly growing cylinder fusion avoids every member of any countable closed-nowhere-dense family; singletons qualify.
AC and transfinite recursion give kappa distinct points avoiding all earlier forbidden closed sets.
Each closed nowhere dense set meets L only in an initial countable set of choices; arbitrary meager sets follow by countable union.
An uncountable subset of a Luzin set has closure containing a cylinder; any uncountable Luzin set supplies a kappa-sized subset.
inputs: a nowhere dense closure would contradict the Luzin property

derivations.claim: Removing rationals leaves an uncountable Luzin set in the irrational subspace, since relative nowhere dense sets have nowhere dense real closures.
inputs: relative closure is the trace of ambient closure

derivations.claim: The Baire/irrational homeomorphism transfers the real-line branch, completing all Luzin and cylinder conclusions.
inputs: homeomorphisms preserve closures, interiors and countable unions
